messages:
incident-bot: P1: GPU backlog spike detected for tenant customer-prod-vpc-12 (us-west2). queue_depth=237 avg_wait=51s autoscaler=throttle
sara: starting incident thread. paging oncall now. @mike please join — looks like private autoscaler is not making progress.
mike: oncall here. first pass: are nodes failing to boot or are we hitting provider capacity/quota limits?
alex: logs show repeated `node_boot_timeout` and `bootstrap: imagePullBackOff` during init. posting autoscaler excerpt:
```
[autoscaler] desired=14 current=8 maxNodes=8 -> rejected (exceeded maxNodes)
[autoscaler] launchAttempt: instanceType=g5.xlarge image=ami-custom-2025-06 bootTimeout=120s
[provider] InsufficientInstanceCapacity: cannot satisfy request for g5.xlarge in us-west2
```
lia: customer uses a locked AMI with extra init steps (kms + registry auth). If cloud-init stalls, kubelet never becomes Ready.
sara: run `kubectl get nodes -l redwood/customer=customer-prod -o wide` and paste.
mike: `8 Ready, 4 NotReady (Init), 2 Pending`. Kubelet logs on Pending show `pull failed: 429 Too Many Requests` from our private registry.
eng-oncall-bot: Suggested mitigations: A) route portion of traffic to hosted fallback, B) increase Dedicated capacity for customer, C) manual node reprovision with generic AMI. Mark which we choose.
sara: do A first (less risk). alex, can you apply a 35% fallback route to hosted?
alex: applying: `routing.apply --tenant=customer-prod --fallback=hosted --percent=35` -> propagated. Monitoring traffic shift.
customer-success-bot: Sending proactive notification to customer success / CS Ops with templated status note.
lia: meanwhile I'm baking a new generic AMI with pre-pulled images and minimal init. Will use it for emergency boot to avoid registry pulls. ETA ~20m to AMI ready and propagate to us-west2.
mike: also request temporary capacity reservation with cloud provider for g5 in us-west2. alex, can you open provider support ticket and request spare capacity?
alex: opened request: SR-32456. provider response: best-effort reservation pending; also flagged region-level scarcity. Initiated spot-check for other zones as fallback.
eng-sre: set tenant inflight cap to protect cluster: `redwoodctl tenant set-inflight customer-prod 60` to throttle new inflight requests.
sara: applied throttle. That will increase 429s but prevent full queuing and cascading timeouts.
eng-sre: also saw registry rate-limit spikes in control plane logs. If many nodes pull at once, pulls are being throttled. Prebaked AMI and smaller rollout should help.
lia: AMI build finished and uploaded to us-west2: ami-emer-2025-06. Starting small batch rollout: 4 nodes with generic AMI to unblock.
mike: watch for `NodeReady` events. If nodes come up, autoscaler can reach desired.
alex: provider confirmed temporary capacity grant of 3 instances; still short of desired but helps. Queue_depth trending down: 237 -> 112 -> 46 since fallback + throttle + manual nodes.
sara: good. keep hosted fallback until cluster stable and inflight back to normal. Start incident ticket and timeline.
incident-bot: Incident P1 acknowledged and ticket 5342 created. Logging timeline.
eng-sre: postmortem items: 1) AMI bootstrap fragility (customer custom AMI + registry auth), 2) provider capacity scarcity handling in autoscaler (reject vs queue), 3) improve fallback automation to shift traffic faster, 4) rate-limit awareness in bootstrap (backoff pulls).
sara: oncall handoff in 45m to @matt if unresolved. Assign follow-ups to eng-sre and platform.
alex: will follow up with provider and CS. lia will coordinate AMI changes with customer.
mike: final note — consider adding soft autoscale override when provider reports InsufficientInstanceCapacity so we can proactively shift traffic before queue hits P1.
sara: agreed. closing active remediation. continue monitoring for 30m then move to post-incident review. :white_check_mark:
